o.text: Borrowed from Arabic وَالِدَيْن (wālidayn), oblique dual of وَالِد (wālid, “father, parent”). The Arabic form already means “parents”, but was additionally suffixed with the Azerbaijani plural ending, and the singular meaning “parent” was then backformed. Related with övlad (“child”), which is from the same Arabic root (and also a backformed singular).
Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish پورتقال (portakal, “orange”), which, in non-standard dialects, also was pronounced with غ (ğ).
Equivalent to böyü- + -t. Ultimately a derivation from Proto-Common Turkic *bedü- (“to grow, increase”).
Inherited from Proto-Turkic *kȫle. Cognate with Turkish köle (“slave”).
Borrowed from Arabic جِزْيَة (jizya), from Middle Persian 𐭢𐭦𐭩𐭲 (gzyt /⁠gazīd⁠/), 𐭢𐭦𐭩𐭲𐭪𐭩 (gzytky /⁠gazīdag⁠/, “poll-tax”).
Borrowed from Russian фотомеханика (fotomexanika). By surface analysis, foto- + mexanika.
